memory_update.text: DCO should remain in the underfollowed lane for Tier-2/Tier-3 defense manufacturing because it combines defense electronics, structural systems, high-cost-of-failure applications, and backlog sensitivity.
NEU is a hidden defense-materials candidate due to American Pacific/ammonium perchlorate exposure; verify segment contribution and facility concentration before promoting beyond Layer 1.
MOG.A exceeds the preferred small/mid-cap band but has unusually clear subsystem exposure to defense actuation, missile steering, and propulsion-control manufacturing capacity.

Prime contractor revenue growth is not the cleanest expression of this node; sub-tier backlog, capacity expansion, qualification status, and program-specific component exposure are better Serenity signals.

Next pass should search for additional US-listed niche defense electronics, connectors, castings/forgings, propulsion components, energetic materials, inspection/testing, and specialty-distribution names with market caps between $300M and $10B.

node: Tier-2 and Tier-3 defense manufacturing capacity
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around lower-tier defense manufacturing capacity. The strongest underfollowed mappings in this pass are not the primes themselves, but qualified sub-tier suppliers with defense electronics, actuation, missile-material, structural, or high-cost-of-failure manufacturing exposure. Reference prime exposure is included only to anchor demand signals and supplier dependency.
